figures.name: Zeus
figures.one_sentence_intro: Babasını devirip tanrıların başına geçen gök tanrısı; yeminleri, misafirliği ve düzeni korur ama kendi iştahını ve kendi kurallarını çoğu zaman aşar.

membership.note: In every ancient list of the Twelve.

domains.evidence: Hes. Theog. 71-74, 504-506, 687-712; Il. passim (cloud-gatherer, thunderer)

domains.domain: Kingship and the ordering of the cosmos among gods
domains.evidence: Theog. 881-885 (gods urge Zeus to rule, he distributes honours); Il. 15.187-193 (three-way division by lot)
Il. 3.276-280; Od. 9.270-271; Aesch. Suppliants; Hes. Works & Days 327-334
Hes. Works & Days 225-285 (Zeus watches justice and injustice in cities); Il. 16.384-393

domains.domain: Fate: executes but is also constrained by it
domains.evidence: Il. 16.431-461 (Sarpedon: Zeus wants to save his son, Hera reminds him of fate); Il. 22.209-213 (golden scales)

major_myths.title: Overthrow of Kronos; Titanomachy
major_myths.summary: Kronos swallows his children; Rhea hides Zeus in Crete; Zeus frees his siblings, defeats the Titans with the Cyclopes' thunderbolt and the Hundred-Handers, and becomes king.

major_myths.title: Division of the cosmos by lot
major_myths.summary: Zeus, Poseidon and Hades divide sky, sea and underworld by lot; earth and Olympus remain common. Poseidon insists this makes them equal in honour.

major_myths.title: Zeus swallows Metis
major_myths.summary: Warned that Metis would bear a child stronger than he, Zeus swallows her; Athena is later born from his head. He repeats his father's fear of succession, by different means.

major_myths.title: Prometheus and Pandora
major_myths.summary: Prometheus tricks Zeus at Mekone and steals fire; Zeus binds him and sends Pandora with the jar of ills to mortals.
major_myths.variants: Aeschylus makes Zeus a young tyrant; Hesiod frames it as justice against deceit.

major_myths.title: Zeus and the death of Sarpedon
major_myths.summary: Zeus wishes to snatch his mortal son Sarpedon from death; Hera warns that every god would then want the same for their children. Zeus weeps tears of blood and lets him die.

major_myths.title: Zeus's liaisons and Hera's wrath
major_myths.summary: Io, Semele, Europa, Leda, Alkmene, Danae, Ganymede, Callisto and others; several by force or disguise. Hera pursues the women and children.
major_myths.variants: Ovid's Roman retellings dominate the popular versions; archaic sources are terser.

major_myths.title: Lycaon and the flood
major_myths.summary: Zeus, visiting as a guest, is served human flesh by Lycaon; he turns Lycaon into a wolf and floods the earth.

major_myths.title: Zeus and Typhon
major_myths.summary: Gaia's last monstrous child challenges the new order; Zeus burns him down with thunder.

related_figures.relation: wife and sister; principal antagonist within the household
brother; equal by lot, subordinate in practice

source_references.note: Aeschylus' Zeus is markedly harsher than Hesiod's.
Roman; shapes most popular versions of the liaisons.

evidence_status.notes: Core kingship/order/oath material is archaic and consistent. The liaison stories are archaic in outline but their emotional colouring is mostly Ovid. Zeus as 'father of gods and men' is a title of authority, not of tenderness; do not read family warmth into it.

recurring_human_situations.situation: Taking over from a predecessor and fearing you will repeat what they did
Being the one everyone waits on for the final decision
Guaranteeing rules for others that you yourself do not keep
Having to let something you love be lost because saving it would break the arrangement everyone depends on
Distributing shares and discovering that the one who distributes is not one of the equals

tensions.statement: Düzeni korumak ile düzeni elinde tutmak arasında
tensions.note: Not a polarity of good/bad order; the same act slides from one to the other over time.

tensions.statement: Kuralın bekçisi olmak ile kuraldan muaf olmak arasında
Kurtarabileceğin şeyi, herkesin bağlı olduğu düzen adına kurtarmamak
tensions.note: No clean opposite. The myth does not say Zeus was right; it says he wept.

constructive_expressions.expression: Holding a shared order that others can rely on (oaths, hospitality, the protection of the weak who ask)
Distributing spheres rather than owning everything
Bearing the cost of a rule you set, visibly (the tears for Sarpedon)

costly_expressions.expression: Appetite that overrides consent and leaves others to pay (the women, the children, Hera)
Punishing dissent disproportionately to protect one's position
Pre-empting a feared successor: control that repeats the father's fear

boundary_questions.question: Bir düzeni korumak ne zaman o düzeni kontrol etmeye dönüşür?
'Herkesten ben sorumluyum' ne zaman 'herkes bana hesap verir'e dönüşür?
Kuralı koyan kişinin kurala uymaması ne zaman fark edilir — ve kimin tarafından?

possible_fifth_questions.question: Son kararı sen verdiğinde, kararı verirken kimseye danıştın mı?
options: Evet, danıştım ama son söz bendeydi
possible_fifth_questions.discriminates: Solitary decision by structure vs. by habit

possible_fifth_questions.question: Koyduğun kuralı bir başkası çiğnediğinde ne oldu?
possible_fifth_questions.discriminates: Whether the rule protects the order or protects the ruler

possible_reveal_material.distinction: Düzeni korumak ile düzeni elinde tutmak arasında
possible_reveal_material.fragment: İlk bakışta sorumluluk gibi görünüyor; anlattığında ise düzenin sende kalması için ne kadarının gerektiğini kimsenin sormadığı bir yer var gibi.

possible_reveal_material.distinction: Kurtaramamak ile kurtarmamayı seçmek arasında
possible_reveal_material.fragment: Belki asıl ağırlık kaybın kendisinde değil, kaybı önleyebilecekken önlememeyi seçmiş olmanda — ve bunun neye hizmet ettiğini kendine söylemiş olmanda.

interpretation_confidence.notes: Order/control and guarantor/exempt follow directly from repeated episodes. The Sarpedon reading is grounded in a single but explicit scene.

orientation.know_nothing_hint: Zeus'un kapısı, düzeni ayakta tutan ve son sözü söyleyen kişinin hikâyeleridir. Burada güç değil, sorumluluğun nerede kontrole döndüğü konuşulur.

story_doors.text_tr: Herkes son kararı senden bekliyor; sen de kimseye danışamadığını fark ediyorsun.
Düzeni korumak için koyduğun kurala en az uyan kişi sensin ve bunu ilk fark eden sen değilsin.
Payları sen dağıttın; sonra dağıtanın eşitlerden biri olmadığını anladın.
Kaybetmesi gerekeni kurtarabilirdin; kurtarmadın, çünkü o zaman herkes aynısını isterdi.
Yerini aldığın kişiye benzemeye başladığından korkuyorsun; korkunun kendisi seni ona benzetiyor.

overinterpretation_warnings: Never 'you are a leader type / a Zeus'. Zeus is a doorway to situations of order and responsibility, not a description of a person.
The liaison myths include rape and abduction. No story door is written from the perpetrator's position, and no Reveal may recast them as 'passion' or 'charisma'.
Do not map Zeus onto fathers or bosses in general; the myths are about holding a shared order, which anyone in any role may face.
'Father of gods and men' is a title of authority; do not read warmth into it.

figures.name: Hera
figures.one_sentence_intro: Evliliğin ve verilen sözün tanrıçası; kocasının ihanetlerini hiç affetmez ama öfkesi çoğunlukla ona değil, ulaşabildiği kişilere iner.

membership.note: In every ancient list of the Twelve.

domains.evidence: Cult title Teleia; hieros gamos festivals; Il. 14.295-296 refers to their marriage

domains.domain: Queenship; protectress of Argos, Samos, Olympia
domains.evidence: Il. 4.51-52 (her three cities); Heraion of Samos and Argos; Heraia games at Olympia (Paus. 5.16.2-8)

domains.domain: Women's life stages (girl, wife, widow) at Stymphalus
domains.evidence: Paus. 8.22.2 (Pais, Teleia, Chera)

major_myths.title: Persecution of Zeus's lovers and children
major_myths.summary: Io driven by a gadfly; Semele destroyed through a trick; Leto's birth delayed; Heracles' birth delayed and his madness sent; Callisto. The wrong-doer (Zeus) is rarely the target.

major_myths.title: The deception of Zeus (Dios apate)
major_myths.summary: Hera borrows Aphrodite's girdle, seduces Zeus on Ida and has Sleep put him under so Poseidon can aid the Greeks. Cunning as the only lever available.

major_myths.title: Bargaining Troy for her cities
major_myths.summary: Hera tells Zeus he may destroy her three favourite cities whenever he wishes, in exchange for Troy's fall. Grievance priced above her own protégés.

major_myths.title: Hera and Hephaestus
major_myths.summary: Ashamed of her lame son, she throws him from Olympus (Il. 18); later he traps her in a throne and is brought back only by Dionysus. In Hesiod she bears him alone, in rivalry with Zeus.
major_myths.variants: Il. 1.590-594 has Zeus, not Hera, throw Hephaestus.

major_myths.title: Hera bound; the revolt against Zeus
major_myths.summary: Zeus once hung Hera from the sky with anvils on her feet for persecuting Heracles (Il. 15.18-24); she had joined a revolt with Poseidon and Athena (Il. 1.396-406).

major_myths.title: Judgement of Paris
major_myths.summary: Hera offers Paris kingship over Asia; he chooses Aphrodite. Hera's enmity to Troy follows.

related_figures.relation: husband and brother; the wrong-doer she cannot punish directly
rival in the Judgement; lender of the girdle

source_references.note: Cult evidence: Hera as civic protectress is far larger than the 'jealous wife' of epic.

source_references.ref: J. V. O'Brien, The Transformation of Hera (1993)

evidence_status.notes: Epic gives the jealous-wife narrative; cult gives a major civic goddess of marriage and the city with almost no narrative. The two are hard to reconcile; this record follows the narrative for story doors and names the cult as a corrective.

recurring_human_situations.situation: Being the wronged party inside a bond you do not leave
Anger that cannot reach the responsible person and lands on those within reach
Holding the dignity of a position while being humiliated inside it
Trading what you protect for what you resent
Rejecting one's own because they embarrass you, then needing them back

tensions.statement: Haksızlığı yapan ile kızgınlığın ulaştığı kişi arasında
Bağı sürdürmek ile bağın içinde barış bulmak aynı şey değil
tensions.note: The myths never resolve this; Hera neither leaves nor rests.

tensions.statement: Kırgınlığı taşımak ile kırgınlığın kim olduğunu belirlemesi arasında

constructive_expressions.expression: Refusing to accept humiliation quietly; keeping the wrong visible
Guarding the dignity of a bond and of those who keep their word (cult of Teleia)
Using the levers one has when direct confrontation is impossible

costly_expressions.expression: Displaced vengeance: punishing the lovers and children rather than the husband
Grievance priced above one's own protégés
Casting out one's own for causing shame

boundary_questions.question: Bir bağı savunmak ne zaman, bağı bozan kişi hariç herkesi cezalandırmaya dönüşür?
Haklı bir kırgınlık ne zaman kimliğin kendisi olur?
Konumun saygı görmesi ile senin görülmen arasındaki fark ne zaman fark edilir?

possible_fifth_questions.question: Kızgınlığını en son kime gösterdin?
possible_fifth_questions.discriminates: Whether anger reaches its object or is displaced

possible_fifth_questions.question: Bu bağdan ayrılmayı hiç açıkça düşündün mü?
possible_fifth_questions.discriminates: Staying as a decision vs. staying as a given

possible_reveal_material.distinction: Haksızlığı yapan ile kızgınlığın ulaştığı kişi arasında
possible_reveal_material.fragment: Kızgınlık yerinde gibi görünüyor; ama anlattığında, kızgınlığın hedefine değil, ulaşabildiği yere gittiği bir yer var gibi.

possible_reveal_material.distinction: Kalmak ile kaldığın yerde barış bulmak arasında
possible_reveal_material.fragment: Ayrılmamak bir karar; ama kalınan yerde huzur olmaması başka bir şey. İkisi aynı anda doğru olabilir.

interpretation_confidence.notes: Displaced anger is the single most repeated pattern in Hera's narrative material. The 'stay vs peace' reading is grounded but selective: cult Hera does not stay unhappily, she presides.

orientation.know_nothing_hint: Hera'nın kapısı, verilen sözün tutulmadığı bir bağın içinde kalan kişinin hikâyeleridir. Burada kıskançlık değil, kızgınlığın nereye gittiği konuşulur.

story_doors.text_tr: Haksızlığı yapan kişiye değil, ulaşabildiğin kişiye kızıyorsun; bunu sen de görüyorsun.
Ayrılmıyorsun; ama kaldığın yerde de barış yok. İkisini aynı anda taşıyorsun.
Sana verilen söz tutulmadı; sözü hatırlatan tek kişi olmak seni yoruyor.
Kırgınlığın o kadar uzun sürdü ki, artık ondan vazgeçmek kendinden vazgeçmek gibi geliyor.
Konumuna saygı gösteriliyor; sana değil. Farkı sadece sen hissediyorsun.

overinterpretation_warnings: Never 'the jealous woman' or 'the wife type'. Hera's cult made her one of the greatest civic goddesses; the narrative is one author's angle.
Displaced anger is a situation, not a trait. Do not tell a user they 'have Hera's anger'.
Do not gender the door: anyone in any bond (work, family, friendship) can stand in it.
The persecution myths involve victims of Zeus; Reveals must not frame the persecuted as rivals who 'had it coming'.

figures.name: Poseidon
figures.one_sentence_intro: Denizin ve depremin tanrısı; kardeşi Zeus'la eşit pay aldığını söyler ama sözü hep ikinci sırada kalır, kızgınlığı ise yıllarca yön değiştirmez.

membership.note: In every ancient list of the Twelve.

domains.evidence: Od. 5.282-381; Homeric Hymn 22
Il. 20.57-66; epithet Ennosigaios
Il. 23.277-278, 307; Paus. 8.10.2; cult Poseidon Hippios
Apollod. 3.14.1 (salt spring on Acropolis); Amymone (Apollod. 2.1.4)

major_myths.title: Equal by lot, second in practice
major_myths.summary: Poseidon insists to Iris that he is Zeus's equal by lot and will not be ordered about; then yields, resentful, when reminded of Zeus's seniority and strength.

major_myths.title: Contest with Athena for Athens
major_myths.summary: Poseidon strikes a salt spring, Athena plants the olive; the judges award Attica to Athena. In one version Poseidon floods the Thriasian plain in anger.
major_myths.variants: Judges vary: gods, Cecrops, or the Athenians.

major_myths.title: The grudge against Odysseus
major_myths.summary: Because Odysseus blinded Polyphemus, Poseidon's son, Poseidon harries him for years, wrecks his raft, and finally turns the Phaeacians' ship to stone for helping him.

major_myths.title: Building Troy's walls; cheated of pay
major_myths.summary: Poseidon (with Apollo) serves Laomedon for a year and builds Troy's wall; Laomedon refuses payment; Poseidon sends a sea monster.

major_myths.title: The Achaean wall
major_myths.summary: Poseidon complains to Zeus that the Greeks built a wall without sacrificing to the gods and that his own Trojan wall will be forgotten; Zeus tells him to destroy it after the war.

major_myths.title: Minos and the bull
major_myths.summary: Minos vows to sacrifice whatever comes from the sea; Poseidon sends a magnificent bull; Minos substitutes another; Poseidon makes Pasiphae desire the bull — the Minotaur is born.

major_myths.title: Medusa, Demeter, Caenis and others
major_myths.summary: Poseidon rapes Medusa in Athena's temple (Ovid), pursues Demeter who becomes a mare (Paus. 8.25.5-7), Caenis (Ovid Met. 12.189-209). Ovid's Medusa version underlies the popular story of Athena punishing Medusa.

related_figures.relation: brother; equal by lot, senior in practice
rival for Athens; opponent at Troy
pursued; mother of Arion by him

evidence_status.notes: The grudge and rank material is Homeric and consistent. The 'water = emotion' reading found in popular sources has no ancient basis and is excluded. The Medusa-in-the-temple story is Ovid only.

recurring_human_situations.situation: Having real power without the final say, and being reminded of it
Losing a contest and not being able to accept the loss as a loss
A grudge that keeps its direction for years
Being owed something and having the debt grow larger than the sum
Someone entering your territory as if it were theirs

tensions.statement: Güçlü olmak ile son sözün sende olması arasında
Kızgınlığı korumak kendine sadakat mi, kendine zarar mı — mit bunu yanıtlamaz
Alacak ile hesap sorma isteği arasında
tensions.note: Same feeling in different doses; the myths escalate it.

constructive_expressions.expression: Vast carrying capacity; others travel on it
Yielding to a legitimate order when reminded, even resentfully
Insisting that contributions be acknowledged (the wall, the pay)

costly_expressions.expression: Punishing whole peoples for one person's act (the Phaeacians)
Flooding the plain after losing a fair contest
Sexual violence; in Ovid, the victim is then punished by another god

boundary_questions.question: Bir kaybı kabul etmek ile kabul etmiş gibi görünmek arasındaki fark ne zaman ortaya çıkar?
Alacağını istemek ne zaman hesap sormaya, hesap sormak ne zaman cezaya dönüşür?
Kızgınlığın yönü yıllar sonra da aynıysa, bu sadakat mi alışkanlık mı?

possible_fifth_questions.question: Kaybettiğin yarıştan sonra karşı tarafla bir daha konuştun mu?
possible_fifth_questions.discriminates: Loss metabolised vs. loss frozen

possible_fifth_questions.question: Sana borçlu olan kişi borcu inkâr mı etti, geciktirdi mi?
possible_fifth_questions.discriminates: Whether the wound is the money or the disrespect

possible_reveal_material.distinction: Kaybı kabul etmek ile kabul etmiş gibi görünmek arasında
possible_reveal_material.fragment: İlk bakışta mesele bitmiş gibi; ama anlattığında bitmiş görünmesi için harcadığın çabanın kendisi bitmediğini gösteriyor olabilir.

possible_reveal_material.distinction: Güçlü olmak ile son sözün sende olması arasında
possible_reveal_material.fragment: Gücün tartışılmıyor; anlattığında asıl yer, kararın senden geçmediği an gibi görünüyor.

interpretation_confidence.notes: Rank and grudge are repeated across Iliad and Odyssey. The debt reading rests on two episodes.

orientation.know_nothing_hint: Poseidon'un kapısı, gücü büyük ama son sözü olmayan kişinin hikâyeleridir. Burada deniz değil, kabul edilmeyen kayıp ve yön değiştirmeyen kızgınlık konuşulur.

story_doors.text_tr: Bir yarışı kaybettin; kaybı kabul etmek ile kabul etmiş gibi görünmek arasında kaldın.
Sana borçlu olan ödemedi; şimdi hesap sorma isteğin borcun kendisinden büyük.
Kızgınlığın yıllar sonra bile aynı kişiyi buluyor; yeri de yönü de değişmedi.
Alanına biri kendi alanı gibi girdi; senin için mesele mülk değil, sorulmamış olmak.
Eşit olduğunu söyledin; herkes kabul etti; sonra karar yine sensiz alındı.

overinterpretation_warnings: No 'water = emotions / deep feelings' reading; it has no ancient basis and turns the door into astrology.
The sexual-violence myths are recorded but not used as doors; do not romanticise them or write from the perpetrator's position.
Poseidon is not 'the second-in-command type'. The situation of power-without-final-say belongs to no personality.
Do not use the Phaeacian episode to normalise collective punishment as 'strong boundaries'.

figures.name: Demeter
figures.one_sentence_intro: Ekinin ve hasadın tanrıçası; kızı ondan alındığında dünyayı beslemeyi keser, ve kızının ancak bir kısmını geri alabilir.

membership.note: In every ancient list of the Twelve.

domains.domain: Grain, agriculture, the fertility of the tilled earth
domains.evidence: Homeric Hymn 2.302-313, 450-456; Hes. Works & Days 465-469
Homeric Hymn 2.473-482; Isocrates Paneg. 28; archaeology of Eleusis
Hdt. 2.171; Aristophanes Thesmophoriazusae

major_myths.title: The abduction of Persephone and the famine
major_myths.summary: Hades takes Persephone with Zeus's consent. Demeter searches nine days, learns the truth from Helios, withdraws from Olympus, and stops the grain so that mankind would perish and the gods lose their honours. Zeus is forced to negotiate; Persephone returns for two-thirds of the year.
major_myths.variants: The pomegranate seed: eaten unwillingly (Hymn 2.411-413) or of her own accord in later versions; the division of the year varies (one-third / half).

major_myths.title: Demophoön and Metaneira
major_myths.summary: Disguised as an old nurse at Eleusis, Demeter anoints the infant Demophoön with ambrosia and lays him in the fire each night to make him immortal; Metaneira sees and screams; Demeter, furious, abandons the plan and reveals herself.

major_myths.title: Founding of the Mysteries
major_myths.summary: After Persephone's return Demeter teaches the Eleusinian rites to the princes of Eleusis; the initiate is blessed, the uninitiated 'has no share in such good things once dead'.

major_myths.title: Erysichthon
major_myths.summary: He cuts down Demeter's sacred grove to build a hall; she gives him insatiable hunger; he eats his household into poverty.

major_myths.title: Demeter pursued by Poseidon
major_myths.summary: Searching for her daughter, Demeter is pursued by Poseidon; she becomes a mare, he a stallion; Arion the horse and (in Arcadia) Despoina are born. Demeter Erinys.

related_figures.relation: brother; consented to the abduction, then forced to negotiate
paired in vegetation cult; both suffer and return

source_references.ref: H. P. Foley (ed.), The Homeric Hymn to Demeter (1994)

evidence_status.notes: One long archaic hymn carries almost the whole narrative; the content of the Mysteries themselves is unknown and must not be invented. Demophoön is often omitted in popular retellings but is central to the hymn.

recurring_human_situations.situation: Something taken from you with the consent of people who should have protected it
Grief that stops everything, and everyone pays
Getting back only part of what was lost; the rest lives in another life
Trying to protect someone in a way they, or their family, experience as harm
Being noticed only when you stop giving

tensions.statement: Yas olarak durmak ile itiraz olarak durmak — mit ikisini birbirinden ayırmaz, sonuç aynı: kural değişir
tensions.note: Not 'too much vs too little grief'. The famine is both collapse and the only lever that worked.

tensions.statement: Elinde tutmak ile başka bir hayata bırakmak arasında
Korumak ile onun adına karar vermek arasında

constructive_expressions.expression: Grief that forces an unjust arrangement to be renegotiated
Turning loss into something teachable (the Mysteries follow the return)
Sustaining others; the ordinary bread of every day

costly_expressions.expression: Withholding from everyone because of one loss
Imposing one's own idea of protection on a child who is not one's own, in secret
Punishment that consumes the offender's whole household

boundary_questions.question: Bir çocuğun geleceğini korumak ne zaman onun geleceğine karar vermeye dönüşür?
Yas ne zaman herkese karşı bir greve dönüşür — ve grev ne zaman tek işe yarayan şey olur?
Kısmen geri almak ne zaman kabul edilebilir bir barış, ne zaman sürekli bir yara olur?

possible_fifth_questions.question: Durduğun süre boyunca, sana ne olduğunu birine açıkça söyledin mi?
possible_fifth_questions.discriminates: Withdrawal as message vs. withdrawal as collapse

possible_fifth_questions.question: Korumaya çalıştığın kişi ne yaptığını biliyor muydu?
possible_fifth_questions.discriminates: Protection with consent vs. protection imposed

possible_reveal_material.distinction: Yas olarak durmak ile itiraz olarak durmak arasında
possible_reveal_material.fragment: Durmuş olman ikisini de taşıyor olabilir; anlattığında, durmanın kimin için bir mesaj olduğunu kendin de tam söylemiyorsun gibi.

possible_reveal_material.distinction: Elinde tutmak ile başka bir hayata bırakmak arasında
possible_reveal_material.fragment: Geri aldığın kısım gerçek; kalan kısmın başka bir yerde yaşıyor olması da gerçek. İkisini aynı cümlede söylemek zor.

interpretation_confidence.notes: All three tensions come from one hymn, but that hymn is long, archaic, and explicit about motives (Hymn 2.305-313 states the intent behind the famine).

orientation.know_nothing_hint: Demeter'in kapısı, bir şeyi kaybedip her şeyi durduran kişinin hikâyeleridir. Burada annelik değil, kaybın nasıl taşındığı ve neyin geri alınabildiği konuşulur.

story_doors.text_tr: Bir şey senden alındı; sen de her şeye ara verdin. Şimdi bedeli senin dışındakiler ödüyor.
Geri aldın, ama tamamını değil; bir kısmı artık başka bir hayatta yaşıyor.
Onu korumaya çalıştın; o ya da yakınları bunu zorbalık gibi yaşadı.
Beslediğin insanlar seni ancak beslemeyi kestiğinde fark etti.
Kaybın o kadar büyük ki dünyanın devam etmesi sana ihanet gibi geliyor.
Alınmasına razı olanlar sana en yakın olanlardı; kızgınlığın alanla mı, razı olanlarla mı, ayıramıyorsun.

overinterpretation_warnings: Not 'the mother type' or 'nurturing personality'. The door is about loss and withholding; it is open to anyone who has lost anything.
The content of the Eleusinian Mysteries is unknown. Do not invent secret teachings or 'what Demeter learned'.
Do not read the famine as 'emotional blackmail'; the hymn frames it as the only lever against a decision made over her head.
Demophoön must not be flattened into 'overprotective parent'; Demeter is not his mother and acts in secret.

figures.name: Athena
figures.one_sentence_intro: Zeus'un başından zırhlı doğan akıl ve strateji tanrıçası; kahramanlara yol gösterir, döngüleri mahkemeye çevirir, ama ona rakip çıkanı ağır cezalandırır.

membership.note: In every ancient list of the Twelve.

domains.evidence: Born of Metis (Theog. 886-900); guides Odysseus throughout the Odyssey; Il. 22.226-299

domains.domain: Warfare as discipline, as opposed to Ares' frenzy
Crafts: weaving, carpentry, shipbuilding, the bridle
Civic protection of Athens; the olive; law courts
domains.evidence: Hdt. 8.55; Aesch. Eumenides 681-710 (founds the Areopagus court)

major_myths.title: Birth from Zeus's head
major_myths.summary: Zeus swallows Metis; Athena springs from his head fully armed (Hephaestus or Prometheus splits it in later versions).

major_myths.title: Arachne
major_myths.summary: Arachne, a superb weaver, refuses to credit Athena and challenges her. Athena's tapestry shows the gods' majesty; Arachne's shows their crimes against women, flawlessly. Athena tears it, strikes her, and when Arachne hangs herself turns her into a spider.
major_myths.variants: Ovid only; the story has no archaic attestation.

major_myths.title: The trial of Orestes; the Furies persuaded
major_myths.summary: Athena founds the first homicide court, casts the deciding vote for Orestes, then persuades the enraged Furies with honours instead of force, ending the cycle of blood-vengeance.

major_myths.title: Athena deceives Hector
major_myths.summary: Disguised as his brother Deiphobus she lures Hector into facing Achilles, returns Achilles' spear, and vanishes when Hector reaches for a second.

major_myths.title: Mentor of Odysseus and Telemachus
major_myths.summary: Athena steers Telemachus as 'Mentor', reveals herself to Odysseus, arranges the recognition and the slaughter of the suitors, then stops the feud by Zeus's will.

major_myths.title: Medusa and the Gorgoneion
major_myths.summary: Athena aids Perseus and wears the Gorgon's head. In Ovid, Medusa was a beautiful woman raped by Poseidon in Athena's temple and Athena punished her with the serpent hair.
major_myths.variants: Archaic Medusa is monstrous from birth; the punished-victim version is Ovid's.

major_myths.title: Ajax's madness
major_myths.summary: When Ajax sets out to murder the Greek leaders over the arms of Achilles, Athena deranges him so he slaughters cattle instead; she shows Odysseus his humiliation as a lesson in the gods' power.

major_myths.title: Pallas killed; Tiresias blinded
major_myths.summary: Athena accidentally kills her companion Pallas in a sparring match and takes her name (Apollod.); Tiresias sees her bathing and is blinded, though given prophecy in compensation (Callimachus).

major_myths.title: Hephaestus's pursuit; Erichthonius
major_myths.summary: Hephaestus tries to force Athena; his seed falls on the earth; Erichthonius is born and Athena raises him as her own.

related_figures.relation: opposite mode of war; she defeats him twice in the Iliad

source_references.note: Arachne and the punished Medusa are Ovid only.

evidence_status.notes: Mentor, strategist and court-founder are archaic/classical. The two stories most used against Athena today (Arachne, punished Medusa) are Ovidian; kept, flagged.

recurring_human_situations.situation: Being the capable one everyone calls to fix things, and not being asked how you are
Being right and able to win, and seeing what winning will do to the other person
Having to decide in order to end a cycle, knowing either choice loses something
Helping someone so closely that their decisions stop being clearly theirs
Having taken a side while still speaking as the referee

tensions.statement: Haklı olmak ile haklılığın karşındakine ne yaptığını görmek arasında
Yol göstermek ile yönlendirmek arasında
Bir döngüyü bitirmek için karar vermek: hangi tarafı seçersen bir şey kaybolur — mit bunu çözüm değil, çözümün bedeli olarak anlatır
Herkesin üstünde durmak ile herkesin içinde olmak arasında
tensions.note: Parthenos: no bond that binds her. Kept as a tension, not a virtue.

constructive_expressions.expression: Turning vengeance into procedure; persuading instead of forcing
Mentoring: making the other capable rather than doing it for them (Telemachus)
Strategy that spares lives; craft that builds

costly_expressions.expression: Pride that cannot tolerate a rival's excellence, especially when the rival tells the truth
Deceit as strategy against an honourable opponent
Punishing the victim (Ovid's Medusa) or the seer (Tiresias) for what they saw
Humiliating an enemy to make a point to a friend

boundary_questions.question: Yol göstermek ne zaman birinin hayatını yönlendirmeye dönüşür?
Strateji ne zaman aldatmaya dönüşür — ve karşındakinin bunu hak etmemesi neyi değiştirir?
Kendi ustalığın ne zaman başkasının ustalığına tahammülsüzlüğe dönüşür?

possible_fifth_questions.question: Yardım ettiğin kişi, kararın kendisinin olduğunu söylüyor mu?
possible_fifth_questions.discriminates: Mentoring vs. steering

possible_fifth_questions.question: Kazandığında karşı taraf ne yaptı?
possible_fifth_questions.discriminates: A contest that closed vs. a contest that broke someone

possible_reveal_material.distinction: Haklı olmak ile haklılığın ne yaptığını görmek arasında
possible_reveal_material.fragment: Haklılığın tartışılmıyor; anlattığında asıl yer, kazanmanın karşındakine ne yaptığını gördüğün ve yine de devam ettiğin an gibi.

possible_reveal_material.distinction: Yol göstermek ile yönlendirmek arasında
possible_reveal_material.fragment: Yardımın gerçek; ama ne kadarının onun kararı olduğunu sen de tam söyleyemiyorsan, belki asıl soru orada.

interpretation_confidence.notes: Mentor/steer and cycle/verdict follow from archaic and classical texts. Right/kind rests heavily on Ovid's Arachne; Sophocles' Ajax supports it independently.

orientation.know_nothing_hint: Athena'nın kapısı, haklı ve yetkin olan kişinin hikâyeleridir. Burada zekâ değil, yardımın nerede yönlendirmeye ve haklılığın nerede sertliğe döndüğü konuşulur.

story_doors.text_tr: Haklısın ve kazanabilirsin; ama kazanmanın karşındakine ne yapacağını görüyorsun.
Herkes senden çözüm bekliyor; kimse sana nasıl olduğunu sormuyor.
Bir tarafın yanında durdun; artık tarafsız değilsin ama hâlâ hakem gibi konuşuyorsun.
Bir döngüyü bitirmek için karar vermek zorundasın; hangi tarafı seçsen bir şey kaybolacak.
Yardım ederken yön verdin; şimdi ne kadarı onun kararı, ne kadarı senin, bilmiyorsun.
Sana doğruyu söyleyen kişi aynı zamanda sana meydan okudu; hangisine cevap verdiğini bilmiyorsun.

overinterpretation_warnings: Never 'you are the smart one / an Athena'. Competence is a situation here, not an identity.
Parthenos does not mean cold, sexless or 'career woman'; avoid the 'strong independent woman' cliché entirely.
Arachne and the punished Medusa are Ovid's; do not present them as 'the Greek view of Athena'.
The Hephaestus episode is an attempted rape; it is recorded for completeness and is not a story door.

figures.name: Apollo
figures.one_sentence_intro: Kehanetin, müziğin ve şifanın tanrısı; Delphi'de 'kendini bil' der, ama söylediği doğrular çoğu zaman yanlış anlaşılır ve ona meydan okuyanı fazlasıyla cezalandırır.

membership.note: In every ancient list of the Twelve.

domains.evidence: Homeric Hymn 3.281-374; Hdt. 1.46-91; Aesch. Eumenides 1-33
Il. 1.603-604; Homeric Hymn 3.182-206; Hymn 4.464-512 (receives the lyre from Hermes)
Il. 1.43-52 (plague arrows), 1.457-474 (plague lifted); Paian cult; father of Asclepius
Delphic maxims (Paus. 10.24.1: 'know thyself', 'nothing in excess'); Plato Charmides 164d-165a
Identification with Helios is Hellenistic and later (Callimachus fr., Roman poets); in Homer Helios is a separate god.

major_myths.title: Slaying Python; founding Delphi
major_myths.summary: Apollo kills the serpent at the spring, founds the oracle, and takes Cretan sailors as his first priests.

major_myths.title: Cassandra
major_myths.summary: Apollo gives Cassandra prophecy for a promise of love; she refuses him; he makes it so no one will believe her. She foresees Troy's fall and her own death; no one listens.

major_myths.title: Croesus and the ambiguous oracle
major_myths.summary: Told he will destroy a great empire, Croesus attacks Persia and destroys his own. The Pythia replies that he should have asked which empire.

major_myths.title: Marsyas
major_myths.summary: The satyr Marsyas challenges Apollo with the aulos; Apollo wins (in some versions by playing the lyre upside down or singing) and flays him alive.

major_myths.title: Niobe
major_myths.summary: Niobe boasts of her fourteen children over Leto's two; Apollo and Artemis kill them all.

major_myths.title: Daphne
major_myths.summary: Struck by Eros's arrow, Apollo pursues Daphne, who flees and begs her father to change her; she becomes the laurel, which Apollo then claims as his emblem.
major_myths.variants: Pre-Ovidian versions are scarce; the laurel's cult link is older than the story.

major_myths.title: Asclepius killed; Apollo serves Admetus
major_myths.summary: Zeus kills Asclepius for raising the dead; Apollo kills the Cyclopes in revenge; as punishment he serves the mortal Admetus as herdsman for a year, and later wins him a reprieve from death.

major_myths.title: The plague on the Greeks
major_myths.summary: Agamemnon dishonours Apollo's priest Chryses; Apollo shoots plague into the Greek camp until the girl is returned and sacrifice made.

major_myths.title: Hyacinthus
major_myths.summary: Apollo's beloved is killed by a discus (blown by Zephyrus in some versions); Apollo cannot save him and makes the flower.

related_figures.relation: younger brother who steals his cattle and gives him the lyre
shares Delphi in the winter months; classical pairing of measure and release

evidence_status.notes: Prophecy, plague/healing, music are archaic. Daphne's story is essentially Ovid. Apollo as sun god is post-classical; the 'rational Apollo vs irrational Dionysus' pairing is Nietzsche's framing built on a real Delphic sharing, and must be labelled modern.

recurring_human_situations.situation: Seeing clearly what will happen and not being believed, or not being able to save
Saying the truth in a form that does not reach the other person, then asking whose fault the misreading is
Winning a challenge and punishing far beyond the challenge
Approaching someone who experiences the approach as pursuit
Healing and harming with the same hand
Being the one who defines measure for others, and losing measure oneself

tensions.statement: Doğruyu görmek ile doğrunun karşındakine nasıl ulaştığını umursamak arasında
Ölçünün savunucusu olmak ile ölçüyü kaçıranlara ölçüsüz cevap vermek arasında
Uzaktan berrak olmak ile yakında bulanık olmak — yakınlaştığı hikâyelerde Apollon hep kaybeder
Aynı elle iyileştirmek ve zarar vermek — ikisi ayrı yetenek değil

constructive_expressions.expression: Clarity that returns the question to the asker ('you should have asked which empire')
Healing, order, art; lifting the plague when the wrong is repaired
Serving under a mortal after a wrong, and keeping faith with him

costly_expressions.expression: Disproportionate punishment of a challenger
Truth given without regard for how it lands; the gift that becomes a curse
Pursuit of one who does not want him, then claiming her emblem

boundary_questions.question: Doğruyu açıkça söylemek ne zaman doğruyu dayatmaya dönüşür?
Ölçüyü sevmek ne zaman dağınıklığa tahammülsüzlüğe dönüşür?
Yaklaşmak ne zaman kovalamaya dönüşür — ve bunu kim fark eder?

possible_fifth_questions.question: Söylediğin doğruyu karşındaki nasıl karşıladı?
possible_fifth_questions.discriminates: Clarity problem vs. trust problem vs. agency problem

possible_fifth_questions.question: Meydan okuyan kişi kaybettiğinde ne oldu ona?
possible_fifth_questions.discriminates: Contest closed vs. contest turned into punishment

possible_reveal_material.distinction: Doğruyu görmek ile doğrunun ulaşması arasında
possible_reveal_material.fragment: Gördüğün şeyin doğru olması tartışılmıyor; anlattığında asıl yer, doğrunun karşındakine hangi biçimde vardığı ve o biçimin kimin seçimi olduğu gibi.

possible_reveal_material.distinction: Kazanmak ile kazandıktan sonra ne yaptığın arasında
possible_reveal_material.fragment: Yarış bitmiş; ama anlattığında bitmemiş olan şey yarış değil, bittikten sonra devam eden hesap gibi görünüyor.

interpretation_confidence.notes: Clarity/control and measure/excess are repeated across archaic and classical sources. Distance/intimacy is plausible but assembled from three separate stories.

orientation.know_nothing_hint: Apollon'un kapısı, doğruyu gören ama ulaştıramayan kişinin hikâyeleridir. Burada ışık ya da akıl değil, doğrunun nasıl söylendiği ve kazanmanın nerede cezaya döndüğü konuşulur.

story_doors.text_tr: Ne olacağını görüyorsun; söylüyorsun; kimse inanmıyor. Sonra olduğunda kimse sana dönüp bakmıyor.
Doğru söyledin, ama karşındakine ulaşmayan bir biçimde; şimdi hatanın kimde olduğunu bilmiyorsun.
Sana meydan okuyan kaybetti; sen kazandın — ve cezayı fazla kaçırdığını herkes gördü.
İyileştirmeye çalıştığın kişiye aynı elle zarar da verdiğini biliyorsun.
Herkesin ölçüsünü sen koyuyorsun; kendi ölçünü kaçırdığın anı kimse sana söyleyemiyor.
Uzaktan her şeyi net görüyorsun; yaklaştığın her şey bulanıklaşıyor.

overinterpretation_warnings: Apollo is not 'the rational type' and not the sun; both are later layers. Do not pair him with Dionysus as reason vs. emotion — that is Nietzsche, not myth.
Daphne is a pursuit the woman flees. No door is written from the pursuer's position as if it were love; apollo_d6 is about distance, not about her.
Cassandra's door (apollo_d1) puts the user in HER position, not Apollo's. The record keeps the god's cruelty visible.
'Know thyself' is a Delphic maxim, not a Fifth slogan; do not let the UI claim Apollo endorses the product.

figures.name: Artemis
figures.one_sentence_intro: Vahşi doğanın ve avın tanrıçası; kendi alanını, kendi topluluğunu ve henüz büyümemiş olanları korur, ama sınırını aşan kişiye niyetine bakmadan aynı sertlikle karşılık verir.

membership.note: In every ancient list of the Twelve.

domains.evidence: Il. 21.470-471; Homeric Hymn 27; Callimachus Hymn 3

domains.domain: Transitions of girls; childbirth; sudden death of women
domains.evidence: Callim. Hymn 3.20-25; Eur. Hipp. 161-169; Od. 11.172-173, 15.478 (Artemis' arrow as sudden death); Brauron rites (Aristoph. Lys. 641-647)

domains.domain: Protection of the young (animals and children)
domains.evidence: Aesch. Ag. 134-143 (pity for the hare's young); Kourotrophos cult
Identification with Selene is late (Hellenistic/Roman); absent in Homer.

major_myths.title: Actaeon
major_myths.summary: Actaeon, hunting, stumbles on Artemis bathing; she turns him into a stag and his own dogs tear him apart. Ovid stresses it was an accident ('error, not crime').
major_myths.variants: Earlier versions (Stesichorus, Hesiodic frs.) give other motives: boasting, or courting Semele.

major_myths.title: Callisto
major_myths.summary: Callisto, Artemis's companion, is raped by Zeus (disguised as Artemis in Ovid) and becomes pregnant; when the band bathes, her state is seen and Artemis expels her (or turns her into a bear; or Hera does).
major_myths.variants: Who transforms her (Zeus, Hera, Artemis) varies.

major_myths.title: Niobe's daughters
major_myths.summary: With Apollo, Artemis kills Niobe's daughters after her boast against Leto.

major_myths.title: Iphigenia
major_myths.summary: Artemis holds the fleet at Aulis and demands Agamemnon's daughter; in Euripides she substitutes a deer and carries the girl to Tauris as her priestess.
sources: Eur. Iphigenia in Aulis 1540-1612; Iphigenia in Tauris 28-41
major_myths.variants: Aeschylus implies the sacrifice happened; Euripides has the substitution.

major_myths.title: Hippolytus
major_myths.summary: Her devotee Hippolytus is destroyed by Aphrodite's plot; Artemis arrives at his death, explains, promises honours and revenge, and leaves before he dies because gods may not be polluted by death.

major_myths.title: The child Artemis asks Zeus
major_myths.summary: As a small child she asks Zeus for perpetual virginity, many names, a bow, sixty ocean-nymph companions, all the mountains, and only one city.

major_myths.title: The Calydonian boar
major_myths.summary: Oeneus forgets Artemis at the harvest sacrifice; she sends a monstrous boar; the hunt leads to the war over the hide and Meleager's death.

major_myths.title: Orion
major_myths.summary: Orion dies by Artemis: for attempting her, for challenging her at the discus, or by her arrow through Apollo's trick; or by a scorpion. Versions do not agree.

related_figures.relation: opposite in Hippolytus; Aphrodite destroys her devotee
father; grants her wishes; violates her companion

source_references.ref: Euripides, Hippolytus 1283-1443; Iphigenia in Aulis; Iphigenia in Tauris

evidence_status.notes: Punishment-at-the-boundary is consistent across sources; motives (Actaeon, Orion) are not. Childbirth/kourotrophos aspect is well attested in cult and contradicts the flat 'virgin huntress' image. Moon is late.

recurring_human_situations.situation: Someone crosses your line without meaning to, and you answer as if they meant it
Your group has a code; the one who 'broke' it was actually the one wronged, and you cast them out
Insisting on your own territory until no one can reach you
Not being able to stay with someone at the hardest moment because that moment is not yours to be in
Being forgotten once and answering out of all proportion
Protecting the young fiercely, and being the one who takes them

tensions.statement: Sınırı korumak ile sınırda acımasız olmak arasında
Kurala sadakat ile kişiye sadakat arasında
Kendi alanına sahip olmak ile ulaşılmaz olmak — ikisi aynı istekten çıkar
Birini korumak ile onun en zor anında yanında kalabilmek aynı şey değil
tensions.note: Euripides gives a structural reason (pollution); the tension is not a moral failing.

constructive_expressions.expression: Clean boundaries; a life not defined by pairing
Guarding thresholds and the young; pity for what is small (the hare's young)
Naming what happened and who is responsible, at the deathbed

costly_expressions.expression: Punishing the accidental as if intentional
Expelling the wronged to keep the code intact
Absence at the moment of loss
Disproportion: a forgotten sacrifice answered with a war

boundary_questions.question: Bir sınır ne zaman, onu bilmeden geçen kişi için bir tuzağa dönüşür?
Bağımsızlık ne zaman ulaşılmazlığa dönüşür — ve bunu ilk kim fark eder?
Kuralı korumak ne zaman kuralın kurbanını cezalandırmaya dönüşür?

possible_fifth_questions.question: Sınırını aşan kişi, o sınırın orada olduğunu biliyor muydu?
possible_fifth_questions.discriminates: Violation vs. accident vs. unspoken rule

possible_fifth_questions.question: Dışarıda bıraktığın kişi kuralı kendi isteğiyle mi bozdu?
possible_fifth_questions.discriminates: Code-breaker vs. wronged party

possible_reveal_material.distinction: Sınırı korumak ile sınırda acımasız olmak arasında
possible_reveal_material.fragment: Sınırın yerinde; anlattığında asıl yer, sınırı bilmeden geçen kişiye bilerek geçmiş gibi cevap verdiğin an gibi görünüyor.

possible_reveal_material.distinction: Kurala sadakat ile kişiye sadakat arasında
possible_reveal_material.fragment: Kuralı korumak topluluğu korudu belki; ama anlattığında, kuralın bedelini kuralı bozmayı seçmemiş birinin ödediği bir yer var.

interpretation_confidence.notes: Boundary/cruelty and code/person come from repeated, multiply attested episodes. Care/presence rests on one play but that play makes the reason explicit.

orientation.know_nothing_hint: Artemis'in kapısı, kendi alanını ve kendi topluluğunu koruyan kişinin hikâyeleridir. Burada yalnızlık değil, sınırın nerede tuzağa ve kuralın nerede kişiye karşı döndüğü konuşulur.

story_doors.text_tr: Sınırını aşan kişi bunu bilerek yapmadı; sen yine de bilerek yapmış gibi cevap verdin.
Grubunun bir kuralı var; kuralı bozan aslında haksızlığa uğrayan kişiydi ve sen onu dışarıda bıraktın.
Kendi alanın için ısrar ettin; şimdi kimse sana ulaşamıyor ve bunu istemiş miydin bilmiyorsun.
Birine bağlıydın; en zor anında yanında kalamadın, çünkü o an sana göre değildi.
Bir kez unutuldun; cevabın unutulmayla orantılı değildi ve bunu herkes gördü.

overinterpretation_warnings: Not 'the independent woman' or 'the introvert'. Boundaries are a situation; anyone stands in this door.
Virginity here is a cult status, not a psychological trait; and Artemis presides over childbirth, which breaks the 'cold huntress' image.
Callisto is a rape victim. The door places the user as the one who excluded her, so the user can see the cost; never frame Callisto as having 'broken the rule'.
Moon and Selene are late; do not build astrology on Artemis.

figures.name: Ares
figures.one_sentence_intro: Savaşın kaba yüzünün tanrısı; herkes plan yaparken o vurur, sonra herkes onu suçlar — Homeros onu sevmez, ama Homeros'un sevmemesi de bir kaynaktır.

membership.note: In every ancient list of the Twelve, including the Parthenon east frieze.

epithets.meaning: warlike (also a separate war-god at Sparta)

domains.domain: War as violence, frenzy and slaughter (as distinct from Athena's strategy)
Courage and, in one late hymn, the restraint of rage
domains.evidence: Homeric Hymn 8 (late, possibly Proclus, 5th c. CE): asks Ares for courage AND to 'restrain the bitter rush of my soul'

domains.domain: Civic cult at Sparta, Thebes (ancestral), Athens (Areopagus, temple in the Agora)
domains.evidence: Paus. 1.8.4; 3.19.7; Thebes: Cadmus marries Harmonia, Ares' daughter (Apollod. 3.4.2)

major_myths.title: Wounded by Diomedes; Zeus's contempt
major_myths.summary: Athena guides Diomedes' spear into Ares; he runs to Zeus complaining; Zeus calls him the most hateful of the gods, who loves only strife, and heals him anyway.

major_myths.title: Rushing to avenge Ascalaphus
major_myths.summary: Hearing his son Ascalaphus is dead, Ares arms to go to battle against Zeus's ban; Athena physically stops him and strips his armour, saving him from Zeus's wrath.

major_myths.title: Beaten by Athena in the theomachy
major_myths.summary: Ares attacks Athena; she fells him with a boundary stone; he covers seven acres in falling; Aphrodite leads him off and Athena knocks them both down.

major_myths.title: Caught with Aphrodite in Hephaestus's net
major_myths.summary: Hephaestus traps the lovers in an unbreakable net and calls the gods to see; they laugh; Poseidon guarantees Ares will pay the fine.

major_myths.title: Halirrhothius and the first trial
major_myths.summary: Poseidon's son rapes (or attempts) Ares' daughter Alcippe; Ares kills him; Poseidon prosecutes; the gods try Ares on the hill thereafter called the Areopagus and acquit him.

major_myths.title: Children: Phobos, Deimos, Harmonia
major_myths.summary: With Aphrodite he fathers Fear and Panic, and also Harmonia, who marries Cadmus and founds Thebes' line.

major_myths.title: Bound in a bronze jar by the Aloadae
major_myths.summary: The giants Otus and Ephialtes bind Ares in a bronze jar for thirteen months until Hermes steals him out, nearly dead.

related_figures.relation: opposite mode of war; defeats and restrains him

source_references.note: Almost certainly late (Proclus?); the only ancient text to ask Ares for restraint.

source_references.ref: Roman Mars (Augustan cult) is a different, honoured figure — do not import.

evidence_status.notes: Narrative material is almost entirely Homeric and hostile; cult evidence shows a god who was honoured (Sparta, Thebes, Athens). The only 'constructive' textual voice is a late hymn. The record's constructive expressions therefore lean on one legal myth (Areopagus) and one late text; this is thin and is flagged as such.

Being exposed and laughed at; the laughter hurting more than the act
Losing to someone who plans, again
Being needed and despised at once

Kavgada güçlüsün, planda değil; karşındaki bunu biliyor ve her seferinde oradan kazanıyor.

figures.name: Aphrodite
figures.one_sentence_intro: Arzunun ve güzelliğin tanrıçası; istemenin planları nasıl bozduğunu, istenmenin nasıl sahiplenilmeye döndüğünü ve arzuyu reddedenin başına ne geldiğini anlatır.

membership.note: In every ancient list of the Twelve.

domains.evidence: Hes. Theog. 201-206; Homeric Hymn 5; Sappho fr. 1; Il. 3.380-420
Paus. 1.22.3; 1.1.3; inscriptions to Aphrodite Pandemos at Athens
Plato Symposium 180d-e — philosophical construction, not myth

major_myths.title: Birth from the foam
major_myths.summary: From the severed genitals of Ouranos cast into the sea; she comes ashore at Cyprus with Eros and Himeros attending. Homer instead makes her daughter of Zeus and Dione.

major_myths.title: The Judgement of Paris
major_myths.summary: Offered the choice, Paris awards the apple to Aphrodite, who promises him Helen. The war follows.

major_myths.title: Helen compelled
major_myths.summary: Aphrodite snatches Paris from his duel and orders Helen to his bed; Helen protests and is threatened; she goes. The question of Helen's choice is left open by Homer and argued by later writers.

major_myths.title: Anchises and the shame of the goddess
major_myths.summary: Zeus makes Aphrodite desire the mortal Anchises so she can no longer mock the gods for loving mortals; she lies with him disguised, then reveals herself, and is ashamed; she forbids him to tell.

major_myths.title: Caught with Ares
major_myths.summary: Hephaestus's net; the gods laugh; she flees to Paphos.

major_myths.title: Hippolytus destroyed
major_myths.summary: Because Hippolytus scorns her and honours only Artemis, Aphrodite makes Phaedra love him; the false accusation and Theseus's curse kill him. Aphrodite states her motive in the prologue.

major_myths.title: Adonis
major_myths.summary: Aphrodite loves the mortal Adonis; he is killed by a boar; the anemone (or the Adonia festival) commemorates him.

major_myths.title: Pygmalion
major_myths.summary: The sculptor who loves his own statue prays at her festival; she brings it to life.

major_myths.title: Wounded by Diomedes
major_myths.summary: Rescuing Aeneas she is cut on the wrist; Zeus tells her to leave war to Ares and Athena and mind marriage.

related_figures.relation: rival in the Judgement; borrower of her girdle

source_references.note: Ourania/Pandemos as 'two loves' is Pausanias-the-speaker's philosophy, not cult meaning.
Latin novel, 2nd c. CE; not Greek myth. Excluded from doors.

evidence_status.notes: Desire-as-compulsion (Helen), shame (Anchises) and revenge on the refuser (Hippolytus) are archaic/classical. The Psyche story is late Latin. The civic Pandemos cult is real and cuts against a purely erotic reading.

A relationship exposed; laughter; not knowing which hurts more
Loving what you will lose

story_doors.text_tr: İstediğin şey planını bozdu; şimdi 'ben mi seçtim, sürüklendim mi' diye soruyorsun.
İstenmek iyi geliyordu; istenmek ile sahiplenilmek arasındaki çizgiyi geçtiğin anı kaçırdın.
Birini istememen, onun tarafından küçümseme gibi okundu; şimdi bunun bedelini ödüyorsun.
Hoşlandığın kişiyi yakınlarına söyleyemiyorsun; utandığın o mu, sen mi, bilmiyorsun.

Kaybedeceğini bildiğin birini seviyorsun; bilmek sevmeyi azaltmıyor.

The 'heavenly vs. common love' split is Plato's speaker, not myth; do not moralise desire with it.
Cupid and Psyche is a Latin novel; do not present it as Greek Aphrodite.

figures.name: Hephaestus
figures.one_sentence_intro: Ateşin ve zanaatın tanrısı; annesi onu Olympos'tan attı, o da herkesin ihtiyaç duyduğu şeyleri yaparak geri döndü — ama işinin kabul edilmesi kendisinin kabul edilmesi olmadı.

membership.note: In every ancient list of the Twelve; on the Parthenon east frieze.

epithets.meaning: lame in both legs (or: skilled with both hands)

domains.evidence: Il. 18.368-617 (workshop, bellows, golden handmaidens, Achilles' armour); Theog. 570-584 (Pandora's making)

domains.domain: Civic cult at Athens (Hephaisteia, Chalkeia; temple over the Agora) and Lemnos
domains.evidence: Paus. 1.14.6; IG II² 1496; Il. 1.593-594 (Lemnos)

domains.domain: Peacemaking / comic relief among the gods
domains.evidence: Il. 1.571-600 (reconciles Zeus and Hera, gods laugh as he bustles with the wine)

major_myths.title: Thrown from Olympus
major_myths.summary: Hera, ashamed of his lameness, throws him from Olympus; Thetis and Eurynome raise him in a sea cave for nine years where he learns his craft (Il. 18). In Il. 1 Zeus throws him for defending Hera and he lands on Lemnos.
major_myths.variants: Two throwers, two reasons, two landings. Both Homeric.

major_myths.title: The Return of Hephaestus
major_myths.summary: He traps Hera in a throne with invisible bonds and refuses to come back to Olympus to free her; Ares fails to fetch him; Dionysus gets him drunk and brings him back on a mule. Only then does he release Hera.
sources: François Vase (c. 570 BCE) and many Attic vases

major_myths.title: The net
major_myths.summary: Told by Helios of Aphrodite's affair with Ares, he forges an unbreakable net, traps them in bed, calls the gods to witness, and demands his bride-gifts back. The gods laugh; Hermes says he would gladly be so caught.

major_myths.title: Peacemaker in Iliad 1
major_myths.summary: As Zeus threatens Hera, Hephaestus urges his mother to yield, recalls his own fall, pours wine for all; the gods laugh at his bustling and the feast resumes.

major_myths.title: Thetis and the armour of Achilles
major_myths.summary: Thetis, who saved him as an infant, asks for arms for her doomed son; he makes the shield with the whole world on it.

major_myths.title: Making Pandora
major_myths.summary: At Zeus's order he moulds the first woman from earth; Athena dresses her.

major_myths.title: Pursuit of Athena
major_myths.summary: He attempts to force Athena; she repels him; from his seed on the ground Erichthonius is born.

major_myths.title: Wife: Aphrodite or Aglaia
major_myths.summary: Odyssey makes him Aphrodite's husband; Hesiod gives him Aglaia, youngest of the Graces; Iliad shows him with Charis.
major_myths.variants: Irreconcilable; the net story presupposes the Odyssey version.

related_figures.relation: mother who threw him; whom he binds and frees
the one who could bring him back

source_references.ref: François Vase; Attic vases of the Return

evidence_status.notes: The Return survives mainly through fragments and vase painting; its outline is secure. Contradictory throw and marriage traditions are preserved as variants. Athenian cult made him a major civic god; he is not marginal.

Having proof of a wrong and showing it to everyone, and being the one who ends up small
Holding a grudge and waiting for someone to come and fetch you
Defusing a room with a joke and being laughed at as much as with
Making what everyone needs and still standing outside
Repaying the one who saved you, at any cost

Yaptığın şey herkesin işine yarıyor; sen yine de dışarıda kalıyorsun.

figures.name: Hermes
figures.short_label: Arada duran, hiçbir yere ait olmayan
figures.one_sentence_intro: Haberci, yol gösteren, hırsızların ve tüccarların tanrısı; iki taraf arasında herkesin güvendiği kişidir, ama kendi tarafı sorulmaz — ölüleri de o geçirir.

major_myths.title: The cattle theft and the lyre
major_myths.summary: On the day he is born Hermes invents the lyre, steals Apollo's cattle walking them backwards, denies it before Zeus with an infant's innocence, then reconciles Apollo by giving him the lyre and receiving the herds and the caduceus.

major_myths.title: Guiding Priam to Achilles
major_myths.summary: Zeus sends Hermes to escort old Priam through the Greek camp by night to ransom Hector's body; he lulls the guards, brings him in, and leaves before Achilles sees him.

major_myths.title: Leading the souls of the suitors
major_myths.summary: He calls the ghosts of the slain suitors with his wand and leads them, squeaking like bats, to the underworld.

major_myths.title: Messenger to Calypso; helper against Circe
major_myths.summary: He delivers Zeus's order that Calypso release Odysseus, and earlier gives Odysseus the herb moly and the instructions to overcome Circe.

major_myths.title: Zeus's lackey (Prometheus Bound)
major_myths.summary: Sent to extract Prometheus's secret, Hermes is scorned as a servant; he answers with cold professionalism and leaves the Titan to his punishment.

major_myths.title: Killing Argus
major_myths.summary: He lulls the hundred-eyed watchman with stories and pipe, then kills him to free Io.

major_myths.title: Battus
major_myths.summary: An old herdsman who saw the theft promises silence for a cow; Hermes returns disguised and offers a reward for information; Battus tells; Hermes turns him to stone. The god of tricks punishes the informer.

major_myths.title: Giving Pandora her voice
major_myths.summary: At Zeus's order Hermes puts lies, wheedling words and a thievish nature into Pandora.

related_figures.relation: elder brother; victim of the theft, then friend
helped; grandson through Autolycus in some traditions

evidence_status.notes: Messenger, guide, thief and psychopomp are all archaic and coexist. The 'trickster archetype' is a modern comparative category; the Greek Hermes is above all the god of passage.

Carrying a message that is not yours and being blamed as if it were
Keeping every door open so as not to enter any
Demanding honesty from others while living by the exception

major_myths.title: Semele and the double birth
major_myths.summary: Hera tricks Semele into asking Zeus to appear in his true form; the lightning kills her; Zeus sews the unborn child into his thigh and bears him. Raised in hiding, as a girl in some versions, or by nymphs on Nysa.

major_myths.title: Pentheus and Agave (Thebes)
major_myths.summary: Dionysus returns to his mother's city; King Pentheus denies his divinity and tries to imprison him; the women of Thebes, including Pentheus's mother Agave, go to the mountain as maenads; Pentheus, disguised to spy, is torn apart by his mother, who returns carrying his head as a lion's, and sees what it is only when Cadmus makes her look.

major_myths.title: The pirates
major_myths.summary: Tyrrhenian pirates seize a beautiful youth for ransom; the bonds fall off, wine flows on the deck, a lion appears; the pirates leap into the sea and become dolphins; only the helmsman who recognised the god is spared.

major_myths.title: Lycurgus
major_myths.summary: The Thracian king drives off Dionysus's nurses; Dionysus flees to Thetis; Zeus blinds Lycurgus (Homer); later versions have him madly kill his own son and be torn apart by horses.

major_myths.title: Midas
major_myths.summary: For returning his teacher Silenus, Dionysus grants Midas a wish; Midas asks that all he touches turn to gold; food and drink become gold; he begs release and is told to wash in the Pactolus.

major_myths.title: Ariadne
major_myths.summary: Abandoned by Theseus on Naxos, Ariadne is found and married by Dionysus; her crown becomes a constellation.
sources: Od. 11.321-325 (variant: killed by Artemis on Dionysus's word)
major_myths.variants: Odyssey's version has Dionysus cause her death.

major_myths.title: Bringing Hephaestus back
major_myths.summary: Where force (Ares) failed, Dionysus gets Hephaestus drunk and leads him back to Olympus on a mule.

major_myths.title: The women who refused
major_myths.summary: The daughters of Minyas and of Proetus refuse his rites and are driven mad, killing a child among them.

major_myths.title: Zagreus (Orphic)
major_myths.summary: The Titans dismember the infant Dionysus; he is reborn from the salvaged heart. Orphic, late; influential in modern 'dying god' readings.

Recognising or refusing to recognise what is in front of you (the helmsman, Pentheus)

orientation.know_nothing_hint: Dionysos'un kapısı, kendini bırakan ve bırakmayı reddeden kişinin hikâyeleridir. Burada eğlence değil, bırakmanın nerede dağılmaya ve yasağın nerede davete döndüğü konuşulur.

story_doors.text_tr: Bir şeyi kendine yasakladın; o şey seni hazırlıksız yakalayana kadar yokmuş gibi yaşadın.

İstediğin şeyi tam olarak aldın; şimdi ondan kurtulmak istiyorsun.
Yabancı diye dışlanıyorsun; oysa buralısın ve kimse sormadı.
Zorla olmayan şeyi sen yumuşatarak başardın; herkes rahatladı, kimse nasıl olduğunu sormadı.
Karşındaki şeyin ne olduğunu gördün; herkes görmezden gelirken sen 'bu o' dedin ve tek başına kaldın.

overinterpretation_warnings: Not 'the party type' and not a euphemism for addiction; the myths are about denial and release, not consumption.
The 'late foreign god' story is refuted by Linear B; do not repeat it as history.
Apollo-vs-Dionysus as reason-vs-emotion is Nietzsche's framing; the ancient pairing is a shared sanctuary.
Zagreus / 'dying and rising god' is Orphic and late; do not present it as the Greek Dionysus.
Agave's door (d2) is written from her position with care; never present the maenads' violence as 'empowerment'.

figures.name: Hestia
figures.one_sentence_intro: Ocağın tanrıçası; herkes gidip gelirken o kalır, ilk ve son pay onundur, ama hakkında anlatılan hiçbir hikâye yoktur.

membership.note: Ancient lists of the Twelve are not stable. Hestia appears in some (e.g. lists implied by Plato Phaedrus 247a; Olympia's twelve altars per Pindar Ol. 5.5 and Herodorus fr. 34 include her), while the Parthenon east frieze (c. 440 BCE) shows Dionysus and omits her. The popular story that Hestia 'gave up her seat to Dionysus' has no located ancient source; it appears in modern handbooks (e.g. Robert Graves) and is marked unsourced_popular here. Kept as a documented alternate rather than forced in or out.

major_myths.title: Refusing Poseidon and Apollo
major_myths.summary: Both woo her; she swears by Zeus's head to remain a virgin; Zeus grants her the centre of the house and the first portion instead of marriage.

major_myths.title: Firstborn and last-swallowed
major_myths.summary: Eldest child of Kronos and Rhea, hence first swallowed and last regurgitated — 'first and last' (Hymn 5.22 plays on this).

major_myths.title: Priapus (Roman Vesta)
major_myths.summary: At a feast Priapus approaches the sleeping goddess; a donkey brays and wakes everyone. This is Ovid about Vesta; no Greek Hestia parallel.

major_myths.title: Giving up her seat to Dionysus
major_myths.summary: Widely repeated modern claim that Hestia yielded her Olympian seat to Dionysus to avoid conflict. No ancient source located.
sources: R. Graves, The Greek Myths (1955) §27 — modern
major_myths.variants: Unsourced in antiquity; kept only to be marked as such.

evidence_status.notes: Cult presence is enormous (every hearth), narrative presence nearly nil. Every 'story' about Hestia is either two lines in a hymn to another god, a Roman Vesta story, or modern. This record is therefore mostly interpretation, and says so.
